AssociateCollector.name: AssociateCollector
AssociateCollector.documentation: Associates one Collector with this Environment and configures the customer role Continuum uses to authorize access to associated Collector data. The caller must have permission on the Environment and permission to pass the role. Continuum assumes the supplied role and calls GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorization on the requested Collector; only a successful authorization response permits the association. The caller does not need Collector data-access permission. The Environment retains its other Collector associations. Calling again with an existing association is safe and does not create a duplicate.

CreateCodeFinding.name: CreateCodeFinding
CreateCodeFinding.documentation: Ingests a customer-supplied security finding into an environment. Continuum validates the document synchronously against the required overlay fields for the declared format; invalid documents are rejected with a ValidationException. The maximum accepted document size is 256 KB. The environment must have a source configured, and the finding must identify a code location so Continuum can tie it to a repository in the environment's build. Continuum assigns a findingId and stores the verbatim document. When no successful build yet contains the finding's repository, the finding stays SUBMITTED until the next successful build; if that build does not contain it either, the finding is DISCARDED with discardReason SOURCE_REPO_NOT_FOUND.

CreateCodeScan.name: CreateCodeScan
CreateCodeScan.documentation:
Creates an explicit scan request for one environment. CP creates durable work before any queue delivery occurs.

Retrying a request that succeeded, with the same clientToken on the same environment, returns the original scan instead of starting another one. Token handling is not yet atomic: requests with the same token that run at the same time, or a retry after a request that failed partway through, can leave an additional scan, which may end in the FAILED state with a message that it was superseded. Deleting the environment makes its tokens unusable; a later request with one of them returns ResourceNotFoundException.

Each environment can have a limited number of scans in progress at the same time. Once that limit is enforced, a request that would exceed it returns ServiceQuotaExceededException; wait for a scan to finish (ListCodeScans shows each scan's status), then retry.

CreateCollector.name: CreateCollector
CreateCollector.documentation: Creates the Collector for the caller's account. Provisions an AWS Config service-linked recorder using the caller's federated access session and begins recording infrastructure changes.

CreateEnvironment.name: CreateEnvironment
CreateEnvironment.documentation: Creates an environment and starts its validation and any requested provisioning. Storage provisioning and dependency checks may continue after the initial 201 response; use GetEnvironment to observe completion.

CreateIntegration.name: CreateIntegration
CreateIntegration.documentation:
Creates a new integration with an external source provider. Repeating an identical request with the same clientToken returns the original integrationId, integrationArn, and createdAt. Token records are retained for eight hours after success or terminal failure, including after the integration is deleted; replaying a deleted integration's token does not recreate it. An identical request with a retained terminal failure returns the recorded error.

Reusing a token with different parameters returns ValidationException. A fresh token starts a new create attempt; if the name is already owned by another integration, ConflictException includes that integration's identifier. An attempt still in progress may return ThrottlingException with retryAfterSeconds set to 1; retry with the same token and identical parameters.

GitHub authorization codes are single use. Retry an unresolved attempt with its original token and unchanged parameters first. If the service reports a terminal failure, an expired attempt, or a successful token exchange whose integration could not be saved, restart GitHub authorization with a fresh token and authorization code. The service does not checkpoint provider results for recovery by another request.

DeleteCollector.name: DeleteCollector
DeleteCollector.documentation: Deletes the Collector for the caller's account. The Collector first enters PENDING_DELETION, then the service removes its schedule, AWS Config service-linked recorder, versioned S3 bucket, KMS key, and persisted record.

DeleteEnvironment.name: DeleteEnvironment
DeleteEnvironment.documentation: Deletes an environment and its associated resources.

DeleteIntegration.name: DeleteIntegration
DeleteIntegration.documentation: Deletes an integration and releases its name and account quota. Its retained CreateIntegration token receipt can still replay the original result without recreating the integration. Shared provider registrations are retained: deleting one integration does not remove provider access used by another integration. A fresh GitHub CreateIntegration attempt requires a fresh OAuth authorization code and a new clientToken.

DisassociateCollector.name: DisassociateCollector
DisassociateCollector.documentation: Removes one Collector association from this Environment, preserving its other associations. The stored Collector data-access role is cleared when no Collector associations remain. The Environment owner must have permission to disassociate. A current Collector access grant is not required, and the Collector does not need to remain active or present, so stale or revoked associations can be cleaned up.

GetCodeFinding.name: GetCodeFinding
GetCodeFinding.documentation: Retrieves the current state and details of a finding.

GetCodeIssue.name: GetCodeIssue
GetCodeIssue.documentation: Retrieves the current state and details of an issue.

GetCodeIssueArtifact.name: GetCodeIssueArtifact
GetCodeIssueArtifact.documentation: Retrieves one immutable artifact attached to an issue, including its content.

GetCollector.name: GetCollector
GetCollector.documentation: Retrieves the current state of the Collector for the caller's account.

GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorization.name: GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorization
GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorization.documentation: Authorizes an Environment's access to a Collector's data. Continuum calls this operation with the Environment's Collector data-access role before it reads the Collector's inventory, so grant continuum:GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorization to that role and, for a Collector in another account, in the Collector's resource policy. The operation evaluates the action against the exact Collector ARN and the Collector's current resource policy using IAM and the caller's authenticated request context, with environmentArn as the continuum:EnvironmentArn condition key. A successful request returns HTTP 200 with no response members. If access is not granted, the operation returns AccessDeniedException without disclosing Collector existence, ownership, or the policy layer that denied access. The service does not reinterpret the policy using only an account ID.

GetEnvironment.name: GetEnvironment
GetEnvironment.documentation: Retrieves the current state and configuration of an environment.

GetResourcePolicy.name: GetResourcePolicy
GetResourcePolicy.documentation: Retrieves the resource policy attached to a Continuum resource.

ListAssociatedCollectors.name: ListAssociatedCollectors
ListAssociatedCollectors.documentation: Lists the Collectors currently associated with one Environment in ascending collectorId order. Each entry carries the Collector ARN, so a listed association can be passed straight to DisassociateCollector, including when the Collector belongs to another account. An association recorded before Continuum persisted the ARN is omitted from the response, because without the ARN it cannot be acted on.

ListAssociatedEnvironments.name: ListAssociatedEnvironments
ListAssociatedEnvironments.documentation: Lists the Environments currently associated with one Collector in lexicographically ascending environmentArn order. The ARN identifies each Environment across accounts within the Collector's Region.

ListCodeFindings.name: ListCodeFindings
ListCodeFindings.documentation: Lists the findings in an environment in descending findingId order.

ListCodeIssueArtifacts.name: ListCodeIssueArtifacts
ListCodeIssueArtifacts.documentation: Lists the artifacts attached to an issue in descending artifactId order. Content is returned by GetCodeIssueArtifact.

ListCodeIssues.name: ListCodeIssues
ListCodeIssues.documentation: Lists the issues in an environment in descending issueId order.

ListCodeScans.name: ListCodeScans
ListCodeScans.documentation: Lists customer-visible scans for one environment in descending scanRunId order.

ListCollectors.name: ListCollectors
ListCollectors.documentation: Lists the Collectors owned by the authenticated caller's account, including a Collector whose deletion is in progress. A Collector that is still being created is omitted. The account-scoped Collector quota currently permits at most one result, so no result ordering applies.

ListEnvironments.name: ListEnvironments
ListEnvironments.documentation: Lists all environments in your account in descending environmentId order. This complete-inventory operation intentionally has no response filters; see the input documentation for the API standards justification.

ListIntegrations.name: ListIntegrations
ListIntegrations.documentation: Lists the integrations in your account in descending integrationId order.

PutResourcePolicy.name: PutResourcePolicy
PutResourcePolicy.documentation: Creates or replaces the resource policy attached to a Continuum resource.

StartIntegrationAuthorization.name: StartIntegrationAuthorization
StartIntegrationAuthorization.documentation: Starts an OAuth authorization for a new integration and returns the values the caller sends to the provider's authorization endpoint. The authorization belongs to the calling AWS account, can be redeemed once by CreateIntegration from that same account, and expires after ten minutes.

UpdateCollector.name: UpdateCollector
UpdateCollector.documentation: Updates the customer-controlled mutable properties of a Collector. Only the name and Kubernetes cluster IAM role can be changed.

UpdateEnvironment.name: UpdateEnvironment
UpdateEnvironment.documentation: Updates the customer-controlled mutable properties of an environment. Only the name, the environment's S3 integration source and repository selections, its scan frequency, its network policy, and its patch creation policy can be changed.

UpdateIntegration.name: UpdateIntegration
UpdateIntegration.documentation:
Rotates the credentials used by an Amazon S3 integration. Only S3 integrations can be updated; GitHub integrations cannot be modified. The integration's name, provider type, and bucket remain fixed.

The caller must have iam:PassRole permission for the supplied role, including when only the external ID changes. Continuum verifies that the role can be assumed with the requested external ID and can access the existing bucket before saving both credentials atomically. Omitting externalId preserves its current value. Repeating both current credentials leaves updatedAt unchanged, but still requires authorization and access validation.

AccessDeniedException.documentation: The request is not authorized. Verify that your credentials and request signature are valid and that you have permission to perform this action.

fixedInVersion.documentation: The earliest version that resolves the issue, when one is known.

AffectedPackage.documentation: A software package implicated by a finding.

ArtifactCitation.documentation:
A citation supporting a claim: file:line, an HTTP response, or a graph node id.

1024 rather than 512: validation agents cite a span of reasoning rather than a single location, reaching ~930 characters, and an over-long citation drops its entire ReasoningStep — claim included — rather than just the citation.

ArtifactHttpMethod.documentation:
HTTP method recorded on an exploit artifact.

An enum rather than a pattern-constrained string: callers branch on the method, so the full set belongs in the generated SDKs. A producer value outside this set omits the exploit artifact rather than surfacing an unmodeled method.

ArtifactProofBody.documentation:
The body of a proof: executed code, the output it produced, or an annotated source walk.

Its own type rather than ArtifactText because these are whole documents, not fields: observed bodies reach 12.8K of code and 16K of captured output. At most one proof is present per artifact, so a large bound here does not multiply the way ArtifactText's does.

ArtifactText.documentation:
A bounded free-text field in a projected artifact body.

8192 rather than 4096: a validation agent's reasoning claim runs to ~5.6K in practice, and a claim dropped on length takes its whole ReasoningStep with it. Deliberately NOT raised to the proof-body bound — this type is also the member of a 50-entry ReasoningSteps list and of ArtifactHeaders, so its bound multiplies into the worst-case response size.

The product of these bounds is NOT what actually caps a response. Every projected body is read out of one IssueArtifactContent, itself bounded at 5 MiB, so no projection can exceed the size of the content it came from whatever the member bounds permit. Keeping this one modest is about not inflating a typical response, not about the ceiling.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Environment making the association.

clientToken.documentation: Caller-provided token that makes retried association requests idempotent. The first successful request binds the token to the complete Collector ARN, supplied role, and result for at least 24 hours. During that retry window, reusing it with a different request fails with ConflictException. A matching replay still requires the supplied role to have current Collector access. Once authorized, a matching replay returns the stored result without changing association state. Revocation can deny a replay; it does not remove the stored association or its original result.

collectorArn.documentation: The ARN of the Collector to associate with this Environment.

collectorDataAccessRoleArn.documentation: IAM role in the Environment account that Continuum assumes before authorizing access to associated Collector inventory. Every association, including a same-account association, requires this role. The supplied ARN replaces the Environment's previously stored role. The customer is responsible for granting the role access to every Collector that should contribute data.

AssociateCollectorInput.documentation: Specifies the Collector ARN and data-access role to associate with this Environment.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Environment making the association.

environmentArn.documentation: The ARN of the Environment making the association.

associatedCollector.documentation: The Collector identifier and ARN validated by this operation.

AssociateCollectorOutput.documentation: Contains the Environment and the Collector associated by this request.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the associated Collector.

collectorArn.documentation: The ARN of the associated Collector. The account and Region encoded in this ARN identify cross-account and cross-Region associations.

AssociatedCollectors.documentation: One page of the Collectors associated with an Environment. Unlike CollectorArns and CollectorIds — which describe the non-empty input of an association mutation — a page is empty when the Environment has no associations, and its maximum matches the per-Environment association ceiling.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the associated Environment.

environmentArn.documentation: The ARN of the associated Environment. The account encoded in this ARN identifies cross-account associations; association mutations require its Region to match the Collector's Region.

name.documentation: The customer-visible name of the associated Environment.

status.documentation: The current operational status of the associated Environment.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the associated Environment was created.

AssociatedEnvironment.documentation: A summary of one Environment associated with a Collector. This shape intentionally remains distinct from EnvironmentSummary so the two list operations can evolve independently.

AssociatedEnvironments.documentation: One page of Environment summaries associated with a Collector.

AssociationClientToken.documentation: Caller-provided idempotency token for an Environment association request.

AttackFlowId.documentation: Identifier of an attack flow within a validation bundle.

AuthorizationCode.documentation: An OAuth authorization code used during the integration authentication flow.

BuildRepositoryName.documentation: Workspace-safe repository name stored in a Build source manifest.

collectorDetails.documentation: Collector data access configuration. Omitted when no Collector data access role is configured.

sourceConfiguration.documentation: Sources in the shape accepted by CreateEnvironment and UpdateEnvironment.

environmentConfiguration.documentation: Operating policy in the shape accepted by CreateEnvironment and UpdateEnvironment.

latestScan.documentation: The newest scan requested for this environment, if one exists.

CodeConfigurationDetails.documentation: Code-specific environment properties. GetEnvironment returns the source and operating policy; UpdateEnvironment returns Collector details and the latest scan.

CodeFindingSummaries.documentation: A list of finding summaries returned by public code finding APIs.

origin.documentation: Why the scan was created. Always present.

createdAt.documentation: Time at which Continuum accepted the scan request.

completedAt.documentation: Time at which a terminal result was recorded.

failureStage.documentation: Phase this scan failed in. Present only when status is FAILED, and absent for a scan that failed before this field existed.

CodeScanData.documentation:
Complete customer-visible data for one environment scan.

Kept distinct from CodeScanSummary so GetCodeScan can grow independently of ListCodeScans without changing its response contract.

origin.documentation: Why the scan was created. Always present.

createdAt.documentation: Time at which Continuum accepted the scan request.

completedAt.documentation: Time at which a terminal result was recorded.

failureStage.documentation: Phase this scan failed in. Present only when status is FAILED, and absent for a scan that failed before this field existed.

CollectorArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Collector. Format: arn:{partition}:continuum:{region}:{account}:collectors/{collectorId} The resource-id segment is a fresh, randomly generated identifier assigned when the Collector is created — not a fixed or predictable value.

CollectorClientToken.documentation: Caller-provided idempotency token for a Collector creation request.

collectorDataAccessRoleArn.documentation: IAM role that Continuum assumes to authorize its access to associated Collector inventory. Required for nonempty Collector inventory resolution, in the same account or across accounts. This is independent from any S3 source role.

CollectorDetails.documentation: Collector data access configuration returned for an environment.

CollectorId.documentation: The unique identifier for a Collector resource. This is a fresh, randomly generated identifier assigned when the Collector is created — the same value embedded as the resource-id segment of the CollectorArn.

CollectorSummaries.documentation: Collector summaries returned for an authenticated account. The account-scoped Collector quota currently permits at most one result.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the Collector was created.

CollectorSummary.documentation: A summary of a Collector returned in list responses.

CollectorType.documentation: The source collected by a Collector. Additional kinds can be added as they become supported; recorder provisioning remains a service detail.

ConfigRecorderArn.documentation:
ARN of the AWS Config Recorder provisioned by this Collector. Accepts both recorder shapes:

  • Customer-Managed: ...:config-recorder/{name}
  • Service-Linked: ...:configuration-recorder/{name}/{id} (a service-linked recorder ARN from PutServiceLinkedConfigurationRecorder uses the configuration-recorder resource type and carries a trailing id segment).

ConflictException.documentation: The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the resource.

CreateCodeConfiguration.documentation: Source and operating-policy settings for a new code environment.

environmentId.documentation: The environment to ingest the finding into.

ocsfDocument.documentation: The OCSF finding document to ingest, verbatim. Must declare a class_uid Continuum supports (2002 Vulnerability Finding, or 2007 Application Security Posture Finding) and validate against the vendored OCSF JSON Schema for that class, including the Continuum overlay requirements that finding_info.uid be present and that vulnerabilities[0].affected_code[0].file identify the code location. With several repositories in the environment, the file path must begin with the repository name. Maximum size 256 KB. Stored verbatim and normalized into the typed Finding members returned by GetCodeFinding. GetCodeFinding does not return the document itself.

clientToken.documentation: Caller-provided idempotency token. A retry with the same token and an identical finding document replays the original result; the same token with different content is rejected.

CreateCodeFindingInput.documentation: Specifies the environment and the finding document to ingest.

findingId.documentation: The unique identifier assigned to the finding.

title.documentation: The title extracted from the submitted document. Always populated at ingestion.

status.documentation: The finding's current lifecycle status -- SUBMITTED for a newly ingested finding, or the finding's present status when an idempotent retry replays an already-processed finding.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the finding was ingested.

CreateCodeFindingOutput.documentation: Contains the identifier, ARN, title, and initial status of the newly ingested finding.

clientToken.documentation: An optional token identifying one scan request for this environment. SDKs generate a token when omitted. If a request reaches the service without a token, the service generates one for that request, so each request without a token starts a new scan. To retry a request after a lost response, supply the same token on the same environment; once a request with that token has succeeded, a retry returns the original scan. Concurrent requests with the same token, or a retry after a request that failed partway through, can leave an additional scan, which may end FAILED as superseded. A token is bound to its scan for as long as the service retains the scan's build record, with no shorter expiry. Deleting the environment makes the binding inaccessible: a later request with the token returns ResourceNotFoundException.

scan.documentation: The scan run this request created, or the scan run a previous request with the same clientToken already accepted.

type.documentation: Source to collect. Defaults to AWS_COLLECTOR when omitted.

kubernetesClusterRole.documentation: IAM role configuration used to collect Kubernetes cluster metadata. The authenticated caller must be allowed to pass its exact roleArn to Continuum.

clientToken.documentation: Caller-provided token that makes retried create requests return the original Collector rather than creating a duplicate.

CreateCollectorInput.documentation: Creates a Collector for the authenticated caller.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier assigned to the Collector.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the Collector was created.

CreateCollectorOutput.documentation: Contains the identifier and ARN of the newly created Collector.

CreateEnvironmentConfiguration.documentation: Type-specific configuration for a new environment. Omission creates a code environment with the default operating policy and no sources.

configuration.documentation: Type-specific configuration. Omission creates a code environment with the default operating policy and no sources.

CreateEnvironmentInput.documentation: Specifies the name and type-specific configuration of the new environment. Source and operating-policy settings belong to configuration.codeConfiguration.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier assigned to the environment.

status.documentation: The initial status of the environment. Always ACTIVE on successful creation.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the environment was created.

CreateEnvironmentOutput.documentation: Contains the identifier and ARN of the newly created environment.

clientToken.documentation: An optional token identifying one create attempt within the caller's account, Region, and operation. SDKs generate a token when omitted. If a request reaches the service without a token, the service generates one for that request. Each request without a token starts a new attempt. To replay an attempt, supply the same token and identical input. Authorized users and roles in the same account can retry an attempt this way. Token records are retained for eight hours after success or terminal failure, including after deletion of a successfully created integration. Different input with the same token returns ValidationException.

providerConfiguration.documentation: The provider-specific configuration required to create the integration. Only one member may be specified.

CreateIntegrationInput.documentation: Specifies the provider configuration and name for the new integration.

integrationId.documentation: The unique identifier of the created integration.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the integration was created.

CreateIntegrationOutput.documentation: Contains the original identifier, ARN, and creation time of the new or replayed integration. A replay can refer to an integration that has since been deleted.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Collector to delete.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the environment to delete.

integrationId.documentation: The unique identifier of the integration to delete.

DeliveryReason.documentation: Cause of a PATCH delivery's current state; used only by DeliveryState.reason. These are outcomes of one delivery lifecycle, not shared operation error enums. The two existing skip-code wire values are retained for compatibility.

s3.documentation: The S3 object the patch is delivered to.

github.documentation: The GitHub repository the patch is delivered to, including the pull request once it is opened.

DestinationTarget.documentation: Identity only. Future providers may add union members without duplicating state.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Environment whose associations are updated.

collectorArn.documentation: The ARN of the Collector to disassociate from this Environment.

DisassociateCollectorInput.documentation: Specifies the Collector to disassociate from this Environment.

DomainName.documentation: A domain name permitted for build-time dependency resolution.

DomainNames.documentation: A list of permitted dependency domains. Maximum 50 entries.

EnvironmentArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Environment resource, of the form arn:{partition}:continuum:{region}:{account}:environments/{environmentId}.

scanFrequency.documentation: Recurring scan interval: P1D (1 day), P2D (2 days), or P7D (7 days). PT0H disables recurring scans. Defaults to P1D when creating an environment.

patchCreationPolicy.documentation: Whether Continuum creates a patch for a proposed remediation. Defaults to DISABLED.

codeConfiguration.documentation: Configuration and scan state for a code-scanning environment.

EnvironmentConfigurationDetails.documentation: Type-specific configuration and state returned by GetEnvironment and UpdateEnvironment.

EnvironmentId.documentation: The unique identifier for an Environment resource.

status.documentation: The current operational status of the environment.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the environment was created. Preserve the existing EnvironmentSummary.createdAt date-time wire format.

EnvironmentListEntry.documentation: Summary of an environment returned in list responses.

allowedDomains.documentation: Domains that an environment's agent execution may contact.

repository.documentation: Repository selected from that integration in owner/repository form.

defaultBranch.documentation: Branch used when a scan does not choose a more specific revision.

EnvironmentRepositorySource.documentation: One repository selected from a previously-created integration.

EnvironmentRepositorySources.documentation:
Explicit repository selections for an environment.

The number of repositories is governed by an account-level service quota rather than this shape maximum. The quota defaults to 10 so scans maintain useful quality and coverage, and can be higher for some accounts, up to 100.

An environment that already has more selections than the account's current quota remains readable, and an UpdateEnvironment request that leaves repositorySources unchanged keeps those selections without checking them against the quota. Creating or replacing repository selections, and starting a new scan, must satisfy the account's current quota.

integrationId.documentation: Identifier of an S3 integration in the caller's account. The integration supplies the bucket, the read role, and the external ID Continuum uses to read the prefixes.

codePrefix.documentation: Prefix containing source code. Defaults to code/ when omitted.

contextPrefix.documentation: Prefix containing customer-authored context. Defaults to context/ when omitted.

EnvironmentS3IntegrationSource.documentation: An S3 source for one environment, backed by a previously-created S3 integration.

EnvironmentS3Sources.documentation: A list of S3 integration sources. Only one S3 source is supported today; modeled as a list to allow more sources to be supported without a breaking change in the future.

s3Sources.documentation: S3 sources backed by previously-created S3 integrations.

EnvironmentSourceConfiguration.documentation: GA source configuration for code and customer-authored context.

EnvironmentSourcePrefix.documentation: A source prefix. The service normalizes an omitted value to its documented default.

EnvironmentSourceRoleArn.documentation: IAM role assumed by Continuum for environment-level or source-specific access.

EnvironmentStatusMessage.documentation: A human-readable message providing additional context about the current environment status.

ExploitEffect.documentation: The effect validation observed from an exploit payload.

ExploitabilityVerdict.documentation: Whether validation confirmed the vulnerability is exploitable.

FindingArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a Finding resource, of the form arn:{partition}:continuum:{region}:{account}:environments/{environmentId}/code-findings/{findingId}.

FindingBlockingReason.documentation: Why a validator rejected a finding. NONE accompanies a true positive.

FindingCategory.documentation: A vulnerability-taxonomy label: the producer's category, sub-category, or OWASP category. Deliberately unconstrained beyond length -- producers do not share a taxonomy, so this is NOT a stable filter key across finding types. Use cweIds when a stable classification is needed.

FindingClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive token that you provide to make a finding-creation request idempotent.

FindingCodeSnippet.documentation: A code excerpt: the vulnerable fragment, or a validation-evidence snippet.

FindingComplianceCheck.documentation: One compliance check behind a posture finding.

FindingDescription.documentation: Free-form prose about a finding (summary, detailed analysis, rationale, remediation guidance). Capped well below the finding document's own 256 KB limit, since several of these can appear on one finding.

FindingDiscardReason.documentation: Why a finding was not escalated into an issue. Present only when status is DISCARDED.

file.documentation: The file the evidence was found in.

FindingEvidence.documentation: A code citation supporting a validation verdict.

FindingFilePath.documentation: A repository-relative path to the file a finding is about.

FindingId.documentation: The unique identifier for a Finding resource.

FindingListEntry.documentation: One entry in a free-form list carried verbatim from a producer (relevant inputs, reproduction steps, mitigating controls, preconditions, references).

startLine.documentation: 1-indexed first line of the affected range.

endLine.documentation: 1-indexed last line, when the producer reported a range.

FindingLocation.documentation: A code location a finding points at.

FindingLocationList.documentation: One vulnerability rarely spans more than a handful of locations.

FindingOcsfClass.documentation: The OCSF Finding class a submitted document declared. Continuum validates against, and accepts, only these classes; a document declaring any other class_uid is rejected at CreateCodeFinding, so this is a closed set rather than a pass-through of OCSF's full class registry.

application.documentation: The application the posture was assessed against.

control.documentation: The control assessed, and the producer's description of it.

standards.documentation: Standards and requirements the control maps to.

status.documentation: The producer's compliance status, and the enum value behind it.

FindingPosture.documentation: The compliance posture a finding reports, for the Application Security Posture Finding class. Absent for a vulnerability finding.

FindingResource.documentation: A cloud or application resource a finding concerns.

FindingResourceUid.documentation: A resource identifier -- a cloud ARN, a context-graph node id, or whatever identifier scheme the producer uses.

FindingSeverityAdjustment.documentation: A validator's severity conclusion. UNCHANGED means the producer's reported severity stands.

FindingSeverityId.documentation: A finding's severity, on the canonical numeric scale OCSF defines (UNKNOWN=0, INFORMATIONAL=1, LOW=2, MEDIUM=3, HIGH=4, CRITICAL=5, FATAL=6, OTHER=99). Named rather than numeric so callers never map the scale themselves, and identical across producers.

FindingSource.documentation: The system that produced a finding -- Continuum's own scanner, or the product name (falling back to the vendor name) from a customer document's OCSF metadata.product. Distinguishes two customer integrations that share a type.

FindingStatus.documentation: The lifecycle status of a finding as it moves through Continuum's processing pipeline. CONFIRMED and DISCARDED are terminal states -- a CONFIRMED finding is promoted into a separate Issue (not yet implemented), which owns the subsequent remediation lifecycle; the finding's own status does not change after that.

FindingStatusMessage.documentation: A human-readable message providing additional context about the current finding status.

FindingStringList.documentation: A free-form list of strings carried verbatim from a producer.

sourceFindingId.documentation: The producer's own identifier for the finding.

reportedAt.documentation:
When the producer reported the finding -- its own clock, which is not Continuum's ingestion time. createdAt is when Continuum accepted it; these are genuinely different instants and a reader usually wants this one.

For CreateCodeFinding, this is the submitted OCSF document's own top-level time. For findings Continuum's scanner produces, it is the finding's own creation time.

Continuum does not validate it for plausibility: a producer's value is echoed as given, so a timestamp here asserts the unit and format, not that the instant is genuine.

status.documentation: The current lifecycle status of the finding.

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status last transitioned.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the finding was ingested.

scanRunId.documentation: The scan that produced the finding, when it came from one. For a finding Continuum's scanner produced, this is the Continuum scan run (see GetCodeScan). For a finding submitted with CreateCodeFinding, it is the OCSF document's metadata.correlation_uid, when that value is a valid ScanRunId. Absent when the finding did not come from a scan.

discardReason.documentation: Why the finding was not escalated. Present only when status is DISCARDED.

duplicateOfIssueId.documentation: The existing issue this finding duplicates. Present only for the DUPLICATE_OF_* discard reasons.

createdIssueId.documentation: The issue Continuum created from this finding.

completedAt.documentation: When processing finished, whether by creating an issue or discarding. Absent while the finding is still in flight.

filePath.documentation: The file the finding is about, when it has a code location.

FindingSummary.documentation: A summary of a finding returned in list responses. Shares FindingLifecycleFields with the read operations so the list and get projections cannot drift. Carries a lean content subset -- fetch the finding for its full contents.

FindingTitle.documentation: The title of a finding, from the producer's own title -- OCSF finding_info.title, or the scanner's finding title. Length matches the OCSF title constraint.

FindingType.documentation: What kind of finding this is, and who produced it.

confidence.documentation: The validator's confidence, from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive. Advisory: it does not drive Continuum's own routing decisions. The range is enforced server-side, not by a @range trait -- the smithy-rs server SDK does not support range constraints on double shapes (smithy-rs#2007).

mitigatingControls.documentation: Controls the validator found that reduce exploitability.

preconditions.documentation: Conditions exploitation depends on, which bound the severity.

FindingValidation.documentation: A validator's assessment of a finding. Present only when validation actually ran -- absent for finding types that are ingested untested, rather than reporting a verdict Continuum did not reach.

FindingVerdict.documentation: A validator's conclusion about whether a finding is real.

additionalCweIds.documentation: Further CWEs the producer attributed to this same vulnerability.

cvssBaseScore.documentation: The CVSS base score for cveId, when the producer supplies one, from 0.0 to 10.0.

fixCoverage.documentation: The producer's description of how completely a fix is available.

locations.documentation: Every location this vulnerability was reported at.

code.documentation: The vulnerable fragment, when the producer supplied one.

details.documentation: The producer's extended analysis for this vulnerability.

FindingVulnerability.documentation: One vulnerability reported by a finding. A customer document may report several; each carries its own identity, locations and remediation.

FindingVulnerabilityList.documentation: Matches AffectedPackageList: a document reporting more than this is reporting a scan, not a finding.

confidence.documentation: Confidence in this flow's verdict. Absent when out of range.

findingId.documentation: The unique identifier of the finding to retrieve.

type.documentation: What kind of finding this is. Determines which of the type-specific members below are populated.

category.documentation: The producer's vulnerability category. Not a stable filter key across finding types -- see FindingCategory.

owaspCategory.documentation: The OWASP Top 10 category, when the producer supplies one.

lineNumber.documentation: The 1-indexed line the finding is about. Bounds are enforced server-side rather than by a constraint trait: a numeric constraint generates a distinct newtype per enclosing structure, so the same concept would not share a type across the create input and the read output.

cveId.documentation: The CVE this finding reports, for software-composition findings. Both code types can carry one: a customer document supplies it under vulnerabilities[].cve, and Continuum's scanner reports CVEs for dependency-manifest findings.

cvssBaseScore.documentation: The CVSS base score accompanying cveId, when the producer supplies one, from 0.0 to 10.0. Not computed by Continuum. The range is enforced server-side, not by a @range trait -- the smithy-rs server SDK does not support range constraints on double shapes (smithy-rs#2007).

stepsToReproduce.documentation: Steps to reproduce or exploit the finding.

validation.documentation: The validator's assessment. Absent when no validation ran.

endLine.documentation: The last line of the affected range, from the document's affected_code[].end_line.

mitreTechniques.documentation: MITRE ATT&CK technique identifiers, from the document's finding_info.attacks[].technique.uid.

ocsfClass.documentation: The OCSF class the document declared. Determines whether posture is populated.

ocsfSchemaVersion.documentation: The OCSF schema version the producer wrote against (metadata.version).

sourceStatus.documentation: The producer's own status for the finding, and the enum value behind it. Distinct from status, which is Continuum's lifecycle state -- a producer may call a finding "New" while Continuum has it SUBMITTED.

firstSeenAt.documentation: When the producer first observed the finding (finding_info.first_seen_time). The producer's own clock, not Continuum's.

findingTypes.documentation: The producer's own classification of the finding (finding_info.types).

vulnerabilities.documentation: Every vulnerability the document reported. A document may report several; the flat cveId/cvssBaseScore/filePath/lineNumber members above carry the first one's identity so a caller that only needs "what and where" does not have to walk this list.

posture.documentation: The compliance posture, for an Application Security Posture Finding. Absent for a vulnerability finding.

sourceFindingId.documentation: The producer's own identifier for the finding.

reportedAt.documentation:
When the producer reported the finding -- its own clock, which is not Continuum's ingestion time. createdAt is when Continuum accepted it; these are genuinely different instants and a reader usually wants this one.

For CreateCodeFinding, this is the submitted OCSF document's own top-level time. For findings Continuum's scanner produces, it is the finding's own creation time.

Continuum does not validate it for plausibility: a producer's value is echoed as given, so a timestamp here asserts the unit and format, not that the instant is genuine.

status.documentation: The current lifecycle status of the finding.

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status last transitioned.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the finding was ingested.

scanRunId.documentation: The scan that produced the finding, when it came from one. For a finding Continuum's scanner produced, this is the Continuum scan run (see GetCodeScan). For a finding submitted with CreateCodeFinding, it is the OCSF document's metadata.correlation_uid, when that value is a valid ScanRunId. Absent when the finding did not come from a scan.

discardReason.documentation: Why the finding was not escalated. Present only when status is DISCARDED.

duplicateOfIssueId.documentation: The existing issue this finding duplicates. Present only for the DUPLICATE_OF_* discard reasons.

createdIssueId.documentation: The issue Continuum created from this finding.

completedAt.documentation: When processing finished, whether by creating an issue or discarding. Absent while the finding is still in flight.

GetCodeFindingOutput.documentation: Contains the current state and details of the requested finding. Which type-specific members are populated depends on type.

issueId.documentation: The issue the artifact is attached to.

artifactId.documentation: The unique identifier of the artifact to retrieve.

mediaType.documentation: MIME type the producer declared for its content.

body.documentation: The artifact body, projected against the shape defined for its artifactType. A type with a defined shape is returned as that structure, and anything else through IssueArtifactBody.raw.

metadata.documentation:
Producer-defined structured metadata, when the producer supplied any.

Returned only for an artifactType whose content has no defined shape, so that the artifact stays inspectable. For an artifactType with a defined shape, body carries the content and this member is omitted.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the artifact was created.

GetCodeIssueArtifactOutput.documentation: Contains the requested artifact and its content.

issueId.documentation: The unique identifier of the issue to retrieve.

severity.documentation: Current severity: the FindingSeverity seed at create, overwritten by the authoritative severity that prioritization assigns after validation.

confidence.documentation: The likelihood that this issue is a true positive, expressed as a percentage (0-100).

severityReasoning.documentation: The justification for the current severity. Always leads with a customer-facing basis clause synthesized from how the severity was determined (e.g. "Severity from finding.", "Severity from Continuum system."); when prioritization has run, its own reasoning follows. Issues created before the basis clause was introduced return their original reasoning without it.

summary.documentation: The remediation completion summary, when the green stage has run.

findingIds.documentation: The findings that motivated this issue. Bare identifiers only -- a caller authorized for GetCodeIssue is not necessarily authorized to read finding detail; call GetCodeFinding for that. Every referenced finding is included regardless of origin (both CustomerUploaded and ContinuumScanner).

status.documentation: The current lifecycle status of the issue.

phase.documentation: The part of the workflow the issue is in. Present when status is IN_PROGRESS, and when status is FAILED and the failing phase is known.

statusReason.documentation: Why the issue failed. Present only when status is FAILED.

statusMessage.documentation: Customer-facing explanation of statusReason. Present only when status is FAILED.

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status or phase last changed.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the issue was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when any field of the issue last changed. Advances on every mutation (including score-only updates that do not transition status), so it is greater than or equal to statusUpdatedAt.

evidenceAvailability.documentation: Whether the issue has any attached evidence (formerly 'artifacts': tool output, remediation proposals, patches). NONE = no evidence; AVAILABLE = at least one evidence item exists. Computed at read time.

patchDelivery.documentation: Customer delivery of the issue's patches, summarized from its PATCH artifacts at read time. Absent when no patch has a destination delivery.

GetCodeIssueOutput.documentation: Contains the current state and details of the requested issue.

accountId.documentation: The AWS account that owns the Collector.

environmentArn.documentation: The full ARN of the Environment requesting the Collector's data. The Environment must be in the caller's account. Continuum supplies this value as the continuum:EnvironmentArn condition key.

GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorizationInput.documentation: Identifies the Collector whose inventory is requested.

GetCollectorDataAccessAuthorizationOutpu.documentation: Empty response returned when the authenticated caller is authorized to access the Collector's data.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Collector to retrieve.

configRecorderArn.documentation: The ARN of the provisioned AWS Config Recorder.

kubernetesClusterRoleArn.documentation: IAM role used to collect Kubernetes cluster metadata.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the Collector was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The time of the last successful UpdateCollector call, returned at whole-second precision in the same date-time format as createdAt.

GetCollectorOutput.documentation: Contains the current state of the Collector.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the environment to retrieve.

status.documentation: The current operational status of the environment.

statusMessage.documentation: Human-readable details about the current status. Present when the status requires additional context (e.g., failure reason).

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status last transitioned.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the environment was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the environment's properties were last updated.

configuration.documentation: Type-specific configuration and state, including code sources, operating policy, Collector details, and the latest scan.

GetEnvironmentOutput.documentation: Contains the current state and configuration of the requested environment.

integrationId.documentation: The unique identifier of the integration to retrieve.

integrationType.documentation: The immutable provider type for the integration.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the integration was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the integration was last updated.

arn.documentation: The ARN of a resource in the caller's account.

authorizationCode.documentation: The OAuth authorization code returned by GitHub after the user authorizes the application.

state.documentation: The state returned by GitHub in the OAuth callback. It must be the state that StartIntegrationAuthorization returned to the same AWS account, and the authorization request must have sent that call's codeChallenge. The state can be redeemed once. A stage that enforces authorization sessions rejects a missing, expired, already used, or other-account state with ValidationException; restart the authorization with StartIntegrationAuthorization.

redirectUrl.documentation: The redirect URL used to obtain the authorization code. Must match one of the redirect URLs registered on the GitHub App. If omitted, the App's default redirect URL is used. Not stored or returned after creation.

GitHubAuthorizationConfiguration.documentation: Write-only OAuth credentials used to authorize a GitHub.com integration. Not stored or returned after creation.

authorization.documentation: OAuth authorization used to establish the integration. Required on create; not returned on read operations.

organizationName.documentation: The name of the GitHub organization to associate with the integration. If not specified, the integration is associated with the authenticated user's personal account.

GitHubConfiguration.documentation: Configuration for a GitHub.com integration using the OAuth authorization code flow.

organizationName.documentation: The name of the GitHub organization associated with the integration.

owner.documentation: The GitHub user or organization that owns the repository.

pullRequestNumber.documentation: Repository-scoped pull request number assigned by GitHub.

headSha.documentation: The head commit SHA of the pull request. Absent until the pull request is opened.

GitHubTarget.documentation: The GitHub repository a patch is delivered to, and the pull request that carries it once opened.

GitLabAccessToken.documentation: A write-only GitLab access token (personal, group or project access token). A type-agnostic bearer token; not stored or returned after creation.

instanceUrl.documentation: The HTTPS base URL of the GitLab instance (gitlab.com or self-managed).

targetType.documentation: Whether the integration targets a group or a single project.

targetPath.documentation: The group or project path the integration targets.

accessToken.documentation: The GitLab access token (personal, group or project). Write-only; not stored or returned after creation. If the token carries the self-rotate scope, rotation is opted in and Continuum manages the token thereafter.

GitLabConfiguration.documentation: Configuration for a GitLab integration using a pasted access token.

instanceUrl.documentation: The HTTPS base URL of the GitLab instance.

targetType.documentation: Whether the integration targets a group or a single project.

targetPath.documentation: The group or project path the integration targets.

tokenRotation.documentation: How the integration's access token is rotated. AUTOMATIC only when the pasted token had the self-rotate scope and rotation was opted in at installation time.

expiresAt.documentation: The expiry of the stored access token, for non-rotating tokens only. A rotated token's original expiry is stale, so this is omitted when tokenRotation is AUTOMATIC.

GitLabInstanceUrl.documentation: The HTTPS base URL of the GitLab instance (gitlab.com or a self-managed instance).

GitLabTargetPath.documentation: The GitLab group or project path (nested, slash-separated), e.g. "my-org/platform/widgets". Each slash-delimited segment must start with an alphanumeric, so .. segments and empty, leading or trailing slashes are rejected.

GitLabTargetType.documentation: Whether the GitLab integration targets an entire group or a single project.

GitLabTokenRotation.documentation: How a GitLab integration's access token is rotated.

IntegrationArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Integration resource, of the form arn:{partition}:continuum:{region}:{account}:integrations/{integrationId}.

IntegrationAuthorizationProviderType.documentation: A provider whose OAuth authorization can be started with StartIntegrationAuthorization.

IntegrationClientToken.documentation: Caller-provided token identifying one Integration creation attempt. Accepts ASCII characters 33 through 126.

IntegrationId.documentation: The unique identifier for an Integration resource.

IntegrationS3ExternalId.documentation: Caller-provided external ID used when Continuum assumes the S3 integration role.

IntegrationS3RoleArn.documentation: IAM role assumed by Continuum to read a customer-managed S3 integration.

integrationType.documentation: The immutable provider type for the integration.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the integration was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the integration was last updated.

IntegrationSummary.documentation: A summary of an integration returned in list responses.

IntegrationType.documentation: The immutable provider type for an integration.

InternalServerException.documentation: The request couldn't be processed because of an internal server issue. Try again later. If the problem persists, contact AWS Support.

IssueArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an Issue resource, of the form arn:{partition}:continuum:{region}:{account}:environments/{environmentId}/code-issues/{issueId}.

prevalidationSignals.documentation:
Projected EVIDENCE content whose stored envelope declares artifact_kind: prevalidation_signals — the severity signals prioritization uses.

One artifactType can select different members here: EVIDENCE also carries the prioritization markdown narrative, which is not JSON and so returns through raw. The member is therefore chosen by artifactType AND, for a type that carries more than one payload kind, the content's own discriminator.

remediationProposal.documentation:
Projected REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL content: a patch the remediation agent produced, with the descriptors needed to apply and verify it.

REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL content that does not match this shape is returned through raw.

patch.documentation:
Projected PATCH content: the remediation patch for one repository, with the descriptors needed to verify and apply it and the state of its delivery to the customer's own bucket or repository.

Every PATCH projects here. The descriptors come from members Control Plane computes or owns when it stores the patch, not from producer metadata, so this member is the whole PATCH contract and metadata is omitted for it.

raw.documentation: The producer's content verbatim, for an artifactType with no defined shape or content that failed to parse against its shape.

IssueArtifactBody.documentation: The projected body of an artifact. The active member is selected by the artifact's artifactType, and for a type that carries more than one payload kind by the stored content's own discriminator; raw carries content for types with no defined shape yet and for content that did not match its shape.

IssueArtifactContent.documentation: Inline artifact content. One shared shape keeps the existing content member and generated SDK type stable across artifact kinds instead of adding a PATCH-only member or changing the wire contract to a kind-specific union. The shared model bound accommodates PATCH; kind-specific limits are enforced by the service after deserialization: PATCH accepts up to 5,242,880 UTF-8 bytes (5 MiB), while non-PATCH kinds, including initial Issue artifacts, are limited to 1,048,576 characters (1 MiB of characters). The wider shared model bound is not the non-PATCH limit. PATCH reads return the raw content from the immutable service copy; storage receipts remain private implementation data.

IssueArtifactId.documentation: Shared identifier for any issue artifact, regardless of kind.

contentSizeBytes.documentation: Size of the artifact content in bytes. The content itself is returned by GetCodeIssueArtifact.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the artifact was created.

IssueArtifactItem.documentation: A summary of an artifact returned in list responses.

IssueArtifactMediaType.documentation: MIME type describing an artifact's inline content, for example text/markdown, application/json, or text/plain.

IssueArtifactProducerName.documentation: Stable name of the agent that produced an artifact.

IssueArtifactType.documentation: The category of an artifact attached to an issue, such as evidence, validation evidence, a remediation proposal, a decision, or a patch.

IssueConfidence.documentation: The likelihood that this issue is a true positive, expressed as a percentage (0-100). Distinct from severity, which measures impact rather than likelihood. Continuum sets this value; callers can't set it.

IssueEvidenceAvailability.documentation: Whether this issue has any evidence (formerly 'artifacts') attached. NONE = no evidence; AVAILABLE = at least one evidence item exists -- call ListCodeIssueArtifacts to retrieve.

IssueFindingIds.documentation: A non-empty list of finding IDs referenced by an issue. Maximum 50 entries. The first entry is the primary finding; later entries are related findings added after it.

IssueId.documentation: The unique identifier for an Issue resource.

status.documentation: The overall result, in priority order: FAILED when any patch's destination delivery failed or exhausted its retries; otherwise PENDING while any is still in progress; otherwise SUCCEEDED when at least one was delivered; otherwise SKIPPED.

patchCount.documentation: Number of the issue's patches that have a destination delivery.

succeededCount.documentation: Number of those patches delivered to their destination.

failedCount.documentation: Number of those patches whose delivery failed or exhausted its retries.

failureReasons.documentation: Distinct reasons of the failed deliveries, in ascending order. Present only when failedCount is greater than zero.

IssuePatchDelivery.documentation: Customer delivery of the patches Continuum produced for an issue, summarized across the issue's PATCH artifacts when the issue is read. Each artifact keeps its own delivery.destination with the full detail; this summary lets a caller see a failed delivery without listing artifacts.

IssuePatchDeliveryStatus.documentation: Overall customer delivery result of an issue's patches.

IssuePhase.documentation: The part of Continuum's workflow an issue is in (IN_PROGRESS) or failed in (FAILED, when known).

IssueRemediationSummary.documentation: A bounded (<=2048) free-form remediation summary distinct from the shorter per-status IssueStatusMessage; carries the green stage's completion synopsis.

IssueSeverityReasoning.documentation: The human-readable justification for the severity prioritization assigned.

IssueStatus.documentation:
The customer-facing lifecycle status of an issue. Coarse by design: phase says which part of Continuum's workflow an IN_PROGRESS (or FAILED) issue is in, and statusReason says why a FAILED issue failed. Distinct from FindingStatus.

Continuum sets this value; callers can't set it.

IssueStatusMessage.documentation: A human-readable message providing additional context about the current issue status.

IssueStatusReason.documentation: Why an issue is FAILED. Present only when status is FAILED.

confidence.documentation: The likelihood that this issue is a true positive, expressed as a percentage (0-100).

status.documentation: The current lifecycle status of the issue.

phase.documentation: The part of the workflow the issue is in. Present when status is IN_PROGRESS, and when status is FAILED and the failing phase is known.

statusReason.documentation: Why the issue failed. Present only when status is FAILED.

statusMessage.documentation: Customer-facing explanation of statusReason. Present only when status is FAILED.

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status or phase last changed.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the issue was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when any field of the issue last changed. Advances on every mutation (including score-only updates that do not transition status), so it is greater than or equal to statusUpdatedAt.

IssueSummary.documentation: A summary of an issue returned in list responses.

IssueSynopsis.documentation: A free-form synopsis of the issue: reasoning, evidence references, and completion criteria. Supplementary evidence and provenance belong in issue artifacts (added via a separate operation) rather than duplicated here.

KubernetesClusterExternalId.documentation: Optional external ID supplied when Continuum assumes the Kubernetes cluster role. This is STS trust-policy context, not a substitute for iam:PassRole.

KubernetesClusterRoleArn.documentation: ARN of the IAM role used for Kubernetes cluster collection. The role must be in the authenticated caller's account and cannot be a service-linked role.

roleArn.documentation: IAM role the authenticated caller passes to Continuum.

externalId.documentation: Optional external ID Continuum supplies when assuming roleArn. This must match the role trust policy when configured and does not replace the caller's iam:PassRole permission.

KubernetesClusterRoleConfiguration.documentation: Complete configuration for the IAM role Continuum assumes to collect Kubernetes cluster metadata.

remove.documentation: Remove the configured role and external ID.

KubernetesClusterRoleUpdate.documentation: One complete mutation of the Collector's Kubernetes IAM role configuration.

nextToken.documentation: Pagination token returned by a prior request.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Collector whose associations to list.

maxResults.documentation: Maximum number of Environment associations to return.

nextToken.documentation: Pagination token for the next page, if present.

nextToken.documentation: A pagination token returned by a previous call. Set to null for the first request; use the returned token for subsequent calls.

nextToken.documentation: A pagination token to retrieve the next page of results. Absent when there are no more results.

ListCodeIssuesOutput.documentation: Contains the list of issue summaries and an optional pagination token.

ListEnvironmentsInput.documentation:
Specifies pagination parameters for listing environments.

Response-filtering justification: filtering is intentionally omitted because every current consumer needs the canonical complete, account-scoped environment inventory, and no useful selective server-side query use case is defined. Environment ID already has the GetEnvironment lookup operation, and status, name, or timestamp filtering is not needed by any current workflow. Adding speculative filters would require unsupported access patterns and ambiguous semantics without reducing data returned for existing consumers. If a concrete indexed query use case is introduced later, its filter values must be bound to pagination tokens so a token cannot be replayed against a different query. The formal API standards decision is recorded in the package-root BR_EXCEPTIONS.md file.

items.documentation: Common metadata for the environments in the account, ordered by environmentId descending.

nextToken.documentation: A pagination token to retrieve the next page of results. Absent when there are no more results.
