OAuthCodeChallenge.documentation: A PKCE code challenge (RFC 7636): the base64url encoding, without padding, of the SHA-256 digest of the code verifier the service keeps.

OAuthState.documentation: An opaque OAuth state value. StartIntegrationAuthorization returns one, and CreateIntegration redeems it, together with the authorization code, for the same AWS account. Sensitive so clients and the service never log it.

PackageManager.documentation: The ecosystem that supplies a package, e.g. "npm", "pip", "maven".

PackageName.documentation: The name of a software package implicated by a finding.

PackageVersion.documentation: A package version string. Not parsed or compared by Continuum -- version syntax is ecosystem-specific.

patch.documentation: The patch exactly as stored, unmodified. Control Plane accepted it only as a text unified diff, so git apply applies it.

format.documentation: The patch's wire format, read from the patch itself, which determines how to apply it. Absent when the patch starts with neither a git mailbox header nor a diff --git header.

repositoryName.documentation: The repository the patch applies to, as named in the source snapshot it was generated against.

patchSha256.documentation:
SHA-256 of the patch's UTF-8 bytes in lowercase hex, computed by Control Plane when it stored the patch.

Lets a caller confirm the patch it applies is byte-for-byte the one that was reviewed. Computed over the patch bytes, so it is verifiable against patch without trusting this value.

sizeBytes.documentation: Size of the patch in UTF-8 bytes, the unit the digest is computed over.

delivery.documentation: Delivery of the patch to the customer's bucket or repository. Absent when the artifact has no delivery destination.

PatchBody.documentation: Projected content for a PATCH artifact: the remediation patch for one repository, with the descriptors needed to verify and apply it and the state of its delivery to the customer's own bucket or repository.

PatchCreationPolicy.documentation: Policy governing whether Continuum creates a patch for a proposed remediation.

status.documentation: How far delivery to the destination has progressed.

target.documentation: Where the patch was or will be delivered. Absent while the destination is still being resolved, or when delivery was skipped before a destination was known.

PatchDelivery.documentation: Delivery of a patch to a destination the customer owns: an object in the environment's source bucket or a pull request in the source repository.

PatchFormat.documentation: How a patch is encoded, which determines the command that applies it.

confidence.documentation: Confidence in this finding's verdict. Absent when out of range.

exploitArtifact.documentation: Exploit artifact produced for this finding, when there was one.

PerFindingResult.documentation: Validation's result for one finding within a multi-finding bundle.

subjectRef.documentation: What this signal is about, such as a finding or issue reference.

dimension.documentation: The axis this signal speaks to. Absent when the producer reported a dimension with no mapping yet.

signalStrength.documentation: The signal's own rating. This is an input to scoring and is NOT the finding's severity.

producerId.documentation: Stable name of the producer that emitted this signal.

confidence.documentation: The producer's confidence in this conclusion, on its native 0-1 scale. Absent when the stored value falls outside 0-1.

confidenceReasoning.documentation: Why the producer is or is not sure, kept structured rather than prose.

computed.documentation: The deterministic values the producer computed from its assessment.

preconditions.documentation: The four exploit preconditions a likelihood signal assessed, each with the basis the producer had for it.

impactDimensions.documentation: The three impact dimensions an impact signal assessed, each with the basis the producer had for it. These are what the computed impact band is derived from.

exploitability.documentation: What validation established about exploitability, on an exploitability signal. This summarizes the verdict the signal was derived from; the proof itself is the VALIDATION_EVIDENCE artifact it cites.

PrevalidationSignal.documentation: One producer's conclusion about one subject on one scoring dimension.

producedBy.documentation: The agent that produced this signal set.

signals.documentation: The signals backing the Issue's proposed severity.

PrevalidationSignalsBody.documentation: Projected content for an EVIDENCE artifact carrying prioritization's prevalidation signals.

ProviderConfiguration.documentation: Provider-specific configuration for creating an integration. Only one member may be specified.

s3.documentation: Public details for a customer-managed S3 integration.

ProviderDetails.documentation: Provider-specific details for an integration. Only one member will be present.

arn.documentation: The ARN of a resource in the caller's account.

policy.documentation: Omit or supply an empty Statement array to clear resource-policy grants and store the canonical empty-statement policy. Cross-account access is denied; same-account access remains subject to identity policies. Use an explicit Deny statement to deny same-account principals too.

expectedRevisionId.documentation: Optional optimistic-concurrency token for the currently observed policy.

PutResourcePolicyInput.documentation: Specifies the resource and its new policy.

step.documentation: Position of this step in the chain.

claim.documentation: The claim or conclusion reached at this step.

confidence.documentation: Confidence in this individual claim, on the producer's native 0-1 scale.

ReasoningStep.documentation: One step in the validation agent's reasoning chain.

RedirectUrl.documentation: An HTTPS redirect/callback URL used during the OAuth authorization flow. Must be one of the redirect URLs registered on the underlying GitHub App.

patch.documentation: The patch exactly as the remediation agent produced it, unmodified.

format.documentation: The patch's wire format, which determines how to apply it. Absent when the producer recorded a format with no mapping yet.

filename.documentation: Filename the producer suggests for the patch, when it named one.

patchSha256.documentation:
SHA-256 of the patch bytes in lowercase hex, as recorded by the producer.

Lets a caller confirm the patch it applies is byte-for-byte the one that was reviewed. Computed over the patch bytes, so it is verifiable against patch without trusting this value.

RemediationProposalBody.documentation: Projected content for a REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL artifact: the patch the remediation agent produced, with the descriptors needed to apply and verify it.

RepositoryName.documentation: The name of a repository in owner/repository format (e.g. acme/payments-api). For an organization-scoped integration, the owner segment must match the integration's GitHub organization (validated at environment creation time). For a personal-account integration, the owner segment is the personal GitHub username and is not validated.

message.documentation: Description of the resource that was not found.

ResourceNotFoundException.documentation: The specified resource was not found. Verify that the resource identifier is correct and that the resource exists.

ResourcePolicyDocument.documentation: A resource policy in displayable JSON form.

ResourcePolicyInputDocument.documentation: A non-empty resource policy document supplied on writes.

ResourcePolicyRevisionId.documentation: Opaque optimistic-concurrency token for a resource policy.

ResourcePolicyTargetArn.documentation: The ARN of a Continuum resource that supports a resource policy. Collectors are the only supported resource type; other well-formed Continuum ARNs are rejected with ValidationException.

roleArn.documentation: Role Continuum will assume to read from the source bucket.

externalId.documentation: Caller-provided external ID required by the role trust policy.

S3Details.documentation: Public details for a customer-managed S3 integration. The sensitive external ID is intentionally omitted.

key.documentation: The object key of the delivered patch.

version.documentation: The S3 version ID of the delivered object, when the bucket is versioned.

S3Target.documentation: The S3 object a patch is delivered to.

ScanClientToken.documentation: Caller-provided idempotency token for an environment scan request.

ScanFailureStage.documentation:
The phase a failed scan was in when it failed.

Present only on a FAILED scan, and absent on one that failed before this field existed. Shares its vocabulary with the non-terminal ScanStatus values so a failure reads directly against the phase sequence, with no mapping.

ScanFrequency.documentation: ISO-8601 duration requested for recurring scans. Supported values are P1D (1 day), P2D (2 days), P7D (7 days), and PT0H (manual scans only). Existing environments with no cadence or a legacy PT6H, PT12H, or PT24H cadence use P1D. Legacy PT48H uses P2D. New requests must use a supported value.

ScanOrigin.documentation: Identifies why a scan run was created.

ScanRunFailureMessage.documentation: Customer-safe failure detail for a scan run.

ScanRunId.documentation: Opaque identifier for a Continuum scan run.

ScanStatus.documentation:
The phase of a scan.

A scan always builds the selected source first and then analyzes the verified result, so the phases below span both halves of the work.

These values are labels, not an ordered sequence for clients to compare. A scan does not necessarily observe every phase — phases are short-lived and a poll can miss one entirely.

message.documentation: Description of the quota that was exceeded.

quotaCode.documentation: The quota code for the exceeded limit.

serviceCode.documentation: The service code for the exceeded limit.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.documentation: The request would exceed a service quota. Review your quota and request an increase if needed.

value.documentation: The level of access exploitation requires. Absent when the producer reported a level with no mapping yet.

missingInfo.documentation: What the producer could not determine, when anything was missing.

SignalAccessPrecondition.documentation: The assessed access-level precondition with the basis behind it.

SignalAttackerGains.documentation: What an attacker gains from exploitation, strongest capability first.

value.documentation: The capability exploitation grants. Absent when the producer reported a value with no mapping yet.

missingInfo.documentation: What the producer could not determine, when anything was missing.

SignalAttackerGainsDimension.documentation: The assessed attacker-gains dimension with the basis behind it.

SignalBand.documentation: A likelihood or impact band on prioritization's shared four-value scale.

SignalBasis.documentation:
Where an assessed value came from, strongest evidence first. A customer weighing an assessment reads this to tell a fact read out of their own code from the producer's inference.

The first three values name a source that states the value directly. The last two do not: INFERRED means the producer reasoned its way to the value, and NO_EVIDENCE_DEFAULT means it had nothing to reason from and used a default.

SignalBlastRadius.documentation: How far the consequences of exploitation reach, widest first.

value.documentation: How far the consequences reach. Absent when the producer reported a value with no mapping yet.

missingInfo.documentation: What the producer could not determine, when anything was missing.

SignalBlastRadiusDimension.documentation: The assessed blast-radius dimension with the basis behind it.

likelihoodBand.documentation: Computed likelihood band, on a likelihood signal.

impactBand.documentation: Computed impact band, on an impact signal.

barriers.documentation: How many of the four exploit preconditions act as barriers (0-4).

SignalComputation.documentation: Deterministic values the producer computed from its assessment, as distinct from the assessment itself.

SignalConfidenceReasoning.documentation: A producer's structured rationale for a signal's confidence.

SignalDimension.documentation: The scoring axis a signal speaks to.

verdict.documentation: Validation's verdict. UNCERTAIN covers a run that was inconclusive — out of budget, an ambiguous failure, or no decisive layer reached — and is never a refutation.

reachedCrownJewels.documentation:
Whether validation reached the high-value sink the attack path posited.

A Boolean rather than an enum: the sink was either reached or it was not, and how far the walk got when it was not is already carried, with more precision, by highestLayerReached. An unknown is the absent member.

highestLayerReached.documentation: The highest impact layer validation reached, 1-5, as a measure of how far the attack path was walked.

confidenceTier.documentation: How strong the evidence behind the verdict is.

scriptable.documentation:
Whether the proven exploit is automatable rather than one-off.

A Boolean for the same reason as SignalPrecondition.value: validation records a bool, and an unknown is the absent member.

sourceValidationArtifactId.documentation: The VALIDATION_EVIDENCE artifact on this same issue holding the proof this verdict summarizes. Fetch it with GetCodeIssueArtifact for the full reasoning chain and exploit artifact.

SignalExploitability.documentation: What validation established about exploitability, as summarized onto the scoring signal derived from it.

targetValue.documentation: How valuable the target is, which can shift the band off its base value.

SignalImpactDimensions.documentation: The three impact dimensions an impact signal assessed. The computed impact band is derived from attackerGains and blastRadius, then shifted by targetValue.

value.documentation:
The producer's determination.

A Boolean rather than an enum, against the Common Terms preference for enums on extensibility grounds. The question each precondition answers is closed — is the code reachable, is configuration required, must a user other than the attacker interact — and the only third state, "not determined", is already expressed by omitting this member, which the projection does whenever the stored value is not a bool. An enum would give two ways to say the same thing, while basis and missingInfo already qualify how firm the answer is.

missingInfo.documentation: What the producer could not determine, when anything was missing.

SignalPrecondition.documentation: One assessed precondition with the basis behind it.

reachableFromAttacker.documentation: Whether the vulnerable code path is reachable by an attacker.

configurationNeeded.documentation: Whether exploitation depends on a non-default configuration.

userInteractionRequired.documentation: Whether exploitation requires a user other than the attacker to take part, for example by opening a link or a file (CVSS User Interaction).

SignalPreconditions.documentation: The four preconditions a likelihood signal assessed.

SignalStrength.documentation: A signal's own rating, an input to scoring rather than a finding severity.

value.documentation: How valuable the target is. Absent when the producer reported a value with no mapping yet.

missingInfo.documentation: What the producer could not determine, when anything was missing.

SignalTargetValueDimension.documentation: The assessed target-value dimension with the basis behind it.

SourceFindingId.documentation: The producer's stable identifier for the finding, extracted from the submitted document. Useful for cross-referencing with the originating system.

providerType.documentation: The provider to authorize. Only GITHUB is supported.

name.documentation: The name the integration will be created with. When specified, the request fails with ConflictException if an integration with this name already exists in the account, before the caller leaves for the provider. The name is only checked: it is not reserved, stored, or authorized. CreateIntegration requires its own name, checks it again, and may use a different one.

StartIntegrationAuthorizationInput.documentation: Specifies the provider to authorize and, optionally, the name the new integration will use.

state.documentation: An opaque value to send as the OAuth state parameter. Pass the value the provider returns in its callback to CreateIntegration as authorization.state.

codeChallenge.documentation: The PKCE code challenge to send as the OAuth code_challenge parameter.

codeChallengeMethod.documentation: The PKCE challenge method to send as the OAuth code_challenge_method parameter.

expiresAt.documentation: The time after which CreateIntegration no longer accepts this authorization.

StartIntegrationAuthorizationOutput.documentation: Contains the values to send to the provider's authorization endpoint.

ThrottlingException.documentation: The request was denied due to request throttling.

sourceConfiguration.documentation: Source changes. s3Sources replaces the environment's S3 source, and repositorySources replaces its repository selections.

environmentConfiguration.documentation: Operating-policy changes. network replaces the environment's network policy; a network without allowedDomains allows no domains. Builds accepted before the change keep the domains they were accepted with. patchCreationPolicy replaces the patch creation policy. scanFrequency updates scan cadence. Omitted members preserve their stored values.

UpdateCodeConfiguration.documentation: Mutable source and operating-policy settings for a code environment.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the Collector to update.

kubernetesClusterRole.documentation: Atomic update to the IAM role configuration used to collect Kubernetes cluster metadata. The set variant requires a complete configuration; the authenticated caller must be allowed to pass its exact roleArn to Continuum. The remove variant clears both the role and external ID.

UpdateCollectorInput.documentation: Specifies the mutable Collector properties. At least one property must be supplied. k8ClusterRole models an atomic set-or-remove mutation, so roleArn and externalId are replaced or removed together.

collectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the updated Collector.

configRecorderArn.documentation: The ARN of the provisioned AWS Config Recorder.

kubernetesClusterRoleArn.documentation: IAM role used to collect Kubernetes cluster metadata.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the Collector was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The time of the last successful UpdateCollector call, returned at whole-second precision in the same date-time format as createdAt.

UpdateCollectorOutput.documentation: Contains the current state of the updated Collector.

UpdateEnvironmentConfiguration.documentation: Type-specific changes to an environment. Omitted members preserve stored values.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the environment to update.

configuration.documentation: Type-specific configuration changes. Omission preserves the configuration.

UpdateEnvironmentInput.documentation: Specifies the mutable environment properties. Supply a name or a change under configuration.codeConfiguration. Its sourceConfiguration.s3Sources and sourceConfiguration.repositorySources replace the S3 source and repository selections. Its environmentConfiguration has patch semantics: omitted members preserve stored values, scanFrequency updates scan cadence, and network and patchCreationPolicy replace the corresponding policies.

environmentId.documentation: The unique identifier of the updated environment.

name.documentation: The current customer-visible name of the environment.

status.documentation: The current operational status of the environment.

statusUpdatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the status last transitioned. Uses the existing GetEnvironment/ListEnvironments ISO-8601 wire format for this field.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the environment was created. Uses the existing GetEnvironment/ListEnvironments ISO-8601 wire format for this field.

configuration.documentation: Type-specific state, including Collector details and the latest scan. Read source and operating-policy settings through GetEnvironment.

UpdateEnvironmentOutput.documentation: Contains the current state of the updated environment. Use GetEnvironment to read its source and environment configuration.

integrationId.documentation: The unique identifier of the S3 integration to update.

providerConfiguration.documentation: The provider-specific changes to apply. The member must match the integration's provider type, and only S3 integrations can be updated.

UpdateIntegrationInput.documentation: Specifies the S3 integration and the credentials to validate and save.

createdAt.documentation: When the integration was created.

UpdateIntegrationOutput.documentation: Contains the current state of the updated S3 integration. The sensitive external ID is omitted.

s3.documentation: Replacement credentials for a customer-managed S3 integration.

UpdateProviderConfiguration.documentation: Provider-specific changes for updating an integration. Only S3 integrations can be updated, so S3 is the only member.

roleArn.documentation: The role to use. Supply the current role when rotating only the external ID. The caller must be allowed to pass this exact role to Continuum.

externalId.documentation: The replacement external ID used when assuming the supplied role. If omitted, the existing external ID is preserved. This value is sensitive and is never included in the public integration response.

UpdateS3Configuration.documentation: Replacement credentials for a customer-managed S3 integration. The bucket cannot be changed.

ValidationConfidence.documentation:
Confidence in a validation verdict, on the producer's native 0-1 scale.

Deliberately unconstrained in the model: the smithy-rs server SDK rejects @range on a double (smithy-rs#2007). The bound is enforced where the value is produced instead — Control Plane projects this from stored content and omits the member when the stored value falls outside 0-1, so an out-of-range producer value never surfaces here as a valid confidence. The rest of the body still projects; only the confidence is dropped.

ValidationConfidenceTier.documentation:
How strong the evidence behind an exploitability verdict is, weakest first.

Modeled as named tiers rather than the producer's 1-4 ordinal: the number alone carries no meaning outside Continuum's own table, and a customer branching on "was this actually run" needs the distinction by name. The declaration order is the ordering.

exploitable.documentation: Exploitability verdict. Explicit UNCERTAIN replaces the producer's tri-state exploitable: true | false | null, so an absent verdict is never confused with a negative one.

terminalStatus.documentation: How the validation run ended. Absent when the producer reported a status with no mapping yet: the rest of the body still projects, so one unmapped enum never costs a customer the whole artifact.

flowVerdicts.documentation: One verdict per attack flow assessed in the bundle.

attackFlowsConfirmed.documentation: Identifiers of attack flows upgraded to Confirmed provenance.

exploitArtifact.documentation:
Concrete payload and its observed effect, when validation produced one by sending an HTTP request.

Only an HTTP proof projects here. A validation agent that proves exploitability by RUNNING code against the repository projects executedProof, and one that proves it by reading the source projects sourceAnalysis. All three are mutually exclusive: at most one is present.

executedProof.documentation: Proof the agent produced by executing code against the repository under test, with the output that execution produced.

sourceAnalysis.documentation: Proof the agent produced by reading the repository's source, with nothing built or run.

perFindingResults.documentation: Per-finding breakdown for a multi-finding bundle. Absent for a single-finding bundle.

ValidationEvidenceBody.documentation: Projected content for a VALIDATION_EVIDENCE artifact: the validation agent's durable proof of exploitability.

code.documentation: The code that was run. Not a request payload: it imports the repository's own modules and drives the vulnerable code path directly.

output.documentation: What the execution printed, including the agent's own PASS/FAIL assertions. Absent when the run printed nothing retained.

observedEffect.documentation: Effect the execution actually produced. observedEffect rather than effect: this one was witnessed, and the name has to stay distinguishable from ValidationSourceAnalysis.inferredEffect, which was not.

ValidationExecutedProof.documentation: Proof of exploitability the validation agent produced by executing code against the repository under test, with the output that execution produced.

httpMethod.documentation: HTTP method the payload was sent with.

responseSnippet.documentation: Leading portion of the response body, bounded by the producer.

ValidationExploitArtifact.documentation: A concrete exploit payload and the effect validation observed from it.

proofCode.documentation: Proof program files, main file first, in their retained order.

ValidationProofCode.documentation: The executed proof's program. Further members, such as command, workingDirectory and supportingInputs, can be added later as optional details.

ValidationProofConsoleOutput.documentation: The retained merged console output; its structure allows optional additions.

content.documentation: The file's non-blank text, exactly as retained.

ValidationProofMaterial.documentation: One proof program file. Further members, such as path and purpose, can be added later as optional details.

ValidationProofMaterialText.documentation: The retained proof file text; its structure allows optional additions.

ValidationProofMaterials.documentation: The proof program's files, bounded so later optional details can be added.

consoleOutput.documentation: What the run printed: standard output and standard error merged, as retained. The text may be empty.

ValidationProofOutput.documentation: Retained run output. Further members, such as completion and outputCompleteness, can be added later as optional details.

ValidationProofSummary.documentation: The Markdown analysis summary; its structure allows optional additions.

summary.documentation: The non-blank analysis as Markdown: the annotated entry-to-sink walk, its citations, and why the checked guards are absent or bypassed.

inferredEffect.documentation: Effect the agent concluded WOULD occur. Deliberately not effect: nothing was executed, so this is reasoned from the source and must not be read as an observation. See ValidationExecutedProof.observedEffect.

ValidationSourceAnalysis.documentation: Proof of exploitability the validation agent produced by reading the repository's source, with nothing built or run. Further members, such as diagram and references, can be added later as optional details.

ValidationTerminalStatus.documentation: How a validation run ended. Producer statuses map onto these; an unmapped status omits terminalStatus while the rest of the body still projects.

documentation: AWS Continuum finds, validates, prioritizes, and remediates code vulnerabilities across the source repositories and AWS resources in your environments.
